correctness.rationale: For a finite local ring Z(R)=M. Anderson--Badawi's theorem gives M as a disjoint clique and decomposes regular residue cosets into K_s components when 2 is in M or opposite-coset K_{s,s} components otherwise, yielding exactly qK_s in residue characteristic two and K_s plus (q-1)/2 K_{s,s} in odd residue characteristic. The component paired-domination enumerators are A_s and B_s. In characteristic two s is even, so the polynomial has least degree 2q, degree qs, and leading coefficient one; in odd characteristic s is odd, so it has least degree q+1, degree qs-1, and leading coefficient s. Fresh independent polynomial calculations reproduced these invariants on representative profiles. The theorem is correct.
